question.:question/problem:
$$
f(y,z)=⟨6{y}^{2},\,y,\,{{selection}}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(y,z)$ above parametrizes the parabolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $x=6{y}^{2}.$ What is the third component of $f?$ Use the named parameters directly as their corresponding Cartesian coordinates.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the named coordinate parameters directly, so the free-axis coordinate is $z.$

For any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨6{y}^{2},\,y,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $y\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $z.$

f(y,z)=⟨{{selection}},\,y,\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(y,z)$ above parametrizes the parabolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $6{z}^{2}=x.$ What is the first component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨6{z}^{2},\,y,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $y\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $6{z}^{2}.$
